**What the original was.** The file was a single 41-byte self-closing root element with no viewBox, no size, no title, and no shapes. Browsers would fall back to a 300 by 150 pixel box and render nothing in it.

**What changed:**

- **Added a viewBox and matching width and height.** The graphic now has an intrinsic 100 by 100 size and scales cleanly when resized, instead of inheriting the browser default box.
- **Added accessibility metadata.** The root carries an image role and points at a title and description, so screen readers announce something meaningful rather than skipping or mislabeling it.
- **Added an XML declaration and a trailing newline.** This improves compatibility with non-browser tools such as Illustrator and Inkscape and keeps the file POSIX-friendly.
- **Kept it free of artwork.** The source had no drawable content, so I did not invent any. The description states that the canvas is empty.

**What was blocked.** Reading the file's extended attributes for provenance, searching nearby directories for related SVGs, checking which rendering tools are installed, and running xmllint all required approval that this session cannot grant.
